pr_body:
Sorry for the wait, here is my long-promised upgrade to PMREM. This has already landed in `<model-viewer>`, but I've done a bunch of work to change it from TS to three's style of JS, and to make it fit the broader use cases of three. I haven't done a change anywhere near this large to three before, so I'm sure this will need some work based on your feedback.

In addition to changing the format of CubeUV, I also made it possible to set environment maps as backgrounds in general. This was necessary for CubeUV, as it yields interpolated backgrounds now for RGBE, but it seemed reasonable to let any style of environment map be used as a background.

This PMREM change gets rid of the sparkles the previous version had and does a pretty accurate job even with extremely HDR environments. It is also notably faster to compute than the old version, and accomplishes this by the use of sequential two-pass spherical Gaussian blurs. I feel like it's always hard to trust an anecdotal perf measurement from the contributor, so if anyone else would like to report loading time differences they observe, I'd love to see them!

Now in addition to creating PMREMs from CubeTextures or Equirectangular textures, you can also provide a scene to render your environment, in case you'd like to avoid the bandwidth cost of an HDR texture.

I think this fixes all of the following issues, but confirmation would be awesome:

Fixes #17911 
Fixes #17855
Fixes #15423 
Fixes #15410 
Fixes #14469 
Fixes #9733
Fixes #8980

review_comments: It seems this new line has broken [webgl_materials_nodes](https://raw.githack.com/mrdoob/three.js/dev/examples/webgl_materials_nodes.html). When this line is called with `MeshStandardNodeMaterial`, a runtime error occurs since the respective `m_uniforms` variable does not have a `opacity` uniform.
I think that be good if we can follow the same standard of check class pattern `material.isMeshPhongMaterial`, `material.isMeshStandardMaterial`...
Ah, sorry about that! I'm not familiar with the nodes system yet. @sunag, are you working on a fix for this, or are you asking me to put up a PR?

No specifically, but at least related, is a redesign of uniforms updates ( https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/18068 ), but it may take too long... 

I like of the simplification of `boxMesh.material.uniforms.tCube.value` to `boxMesh.material.envMap`, the problem is that `ShaderMaterial` use property like `envMap` input to an independent use like `Node` in `NodeMaterial` for example. I think that at the moment is more easy revert the changes of `material.envMap` to `boxMesh.material.uniforms.tCube.value`, otherwise to this work properly is necessary a materialClass to justify a flag specific like `material.isEnvMapMaterial`.

>I like of the simplification of boxMesh.material.uniforms.tCube.value to boxMesh.material.envMap

I do not like it. The box mesh does not have an environment map -- it has a texture. That change has conflated concepts. If it is reverted, that is fine with me.
Justifying a little more... The maily problem that I see is that the `material.envMap` without class approach is a hack for any material including `RawShader` aparently.

Fair enough, but what kind of texture would you put on a skybox besides an environment map? As it was we had a bunch of texture types specific to environment maps that were not usable as skyboxes, so we ended up needing two different textures in memory representing the same image just to have a matching environment and skybox. I'm sure there's a better and clearer way then exactly what I've done, but I'm hoping we can at least find a method that allows for reuse.
I think this solves the issue: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/commit/b1d1f26b19d78b0d792bb86305680d82b2fc9005

@WestLangley I'm responding to your comment here so we can have a thread about it. I found that even when I have shader debugging turned off, compiling the shaders and uploading the attributes takes as much time as running PMREM, hence I'm doing my best not to dispose of anything in case it will be reused. Would it be better to move all these private variables into the constructor as members? Or should I have a dispose method that gets rid of them all? I'm a little fuzzy on best practices in three for class architecture.

Ultimately, I think PMREM should be handled by the renderer and transparent to the user.

In the mean time, the practice has been to call `dispose()` as-needed at the application level.

If we continue to follow that practice in the examples, then users will just copy the pattern.

Okay, I've added a dispose method and updated the examples. Does this look like what you were hoping for? I checked that your example is now back down to the proper number of materials, geometries and textures.
@mrdoob Good call on the flipped cubemaps! I think hard-coding the fix is fine here, since this shader only takes cubemaps as input, right?
